'''''Centaurea calcitrapa''''' is a species of flowering plant known by several common names, including '''common star thistle''', '''red star-thistle'''<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref> and '''purple star thistle'''. It is native to [[Europe]] but is known across the globe as an [[introduced species]] and often a [[noxious weed]].<ref>{{GRIN | accessdate=24 July 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=''Centaurea'' genus part 1|url=http://www.cdfa.ca.gov/plant/ipc/weedinfo/centaurea.htm|archive-url=https://archive.today/20121212041438/http://www.cdfa.ca.gov/plant/ipc/weedinfo/centaurea.htm|url-status=dead|archive-date=12 December 2012|publisher=California Department of Food and Agriculture|accessdate=24 July 2012}}</ref>  The species name ''calcitrapa'' comes from the word ''[[caltrop]]'', a type of weapon covered in sharp spikes.<ref name=uc/><ref>{{Cite journal|doi = 10.1614/0890-037X(2002)016[0452:PSCCSG]2.0.CO;2|issn = 0890-037X|year = 2002|volume = 16|page = 452|title = Purple Starthistle (''Centaurea calcitrapa'') Seed Germination1|last1 = Pitcairn|first1 = Michael J.|last2 = Young|first2 = James A.|last3 = Clements|first3 = Charlie D.|last4 = Balciunas|first4 = JOE|journal = Weed Technology|issue = 2}}</ref>

==Description==
This an annual or [[biennial plant]] growing erect to a maximum height of one<ref>{{cite web|url=http://ucjeps.berkeley.edu/cgi-bin/get_JM_treatment.pl?609,877,878 |title=Jepson Manual Treatment |publisher=Ucjeps.berkeley.edu |date= |accessdate=2013-01-14}}</ref> to 1.3<ref name=uc>{{cite web |url=http://ucce.ucdavis.edu/datastore/detailreport.cfm?usernumber=26&surveynumber=182 |title=University of California Cooperative Extension |publisher=Ucce.ucdavis.edu |date= |accessdate=2013-01-14 |archive-date=2011-09-27 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110927074155/http://ucce.ucdavis.edu/datastore/detailreport.cfm?usernumber=26&surveynumber=182 |url-status=dead }}</ref> metres.

The stems are hairless and grooved.<ref name="The Wild Flower Key">{{cite book |last=Rose |first=Francis|authorlink=Francis Rose  |title=The Wild Flower Key |year=1981 |publisher=Frederick Warne & Co|isbn=0-7232-2419-6 |pages=386–387}}</ref>

It sometimes takes the shape of a mound, and it is finely to densely hairy to spiny. The leaves are dotted with resin glands. The lowermost may reach a length of 20 centimeters and are deeply cut into lobes. The [[inflorescence]] contains a few [[Head (botany)|flower heads]]. Each is 1.5 to 2 centimeters long and oval in general shape. The [[bract|phyllaries]] are green or straw-colored and tipped in tough, sharp yellow spines. The head contains many bright purple flowers. The fruit is an [[achene]] a few millimeters long which lacks a [[Pappus (flower structure)|pappus]].

It flowers from July until September, and the seeds ripen from August to October.

The Red Star-thistle has been identified as a Priority Species by the UK Biodiversity Action Plan. It is identified as 'vulnerable' by the UNIC and is listed as Nationally Rare in the UK Red Data Book. There is no national or Sussex BAP for this species.

==Subspecies==
Three subspecies are accepted.<ref name = powo/>
*''Centaurea calcitrapa'' subsp. ''angusticeps'' {{small|(H.Lindb.) Meikle}} – [[Cyprus]]
*''Centaurea calcitrapa'' subsp. ''calcitrapa'' –  Baltic states, Czech Republic, southeastern Europe, Corsica, Sardinia, Iberian Peninsula, northwestern Africa, Egypt, Sudan, Turkey, Lebanon and Syria, Saudi Arabia, and Iran.
*''Centaurea calcitrapa'' subsp. ''cilicica'' {{small|(Boiss. & Balansa) Wagenitz}} – Turkey

==Uses==
In western [[Crete]], [[Greece]] a local variety called gourounaki (γουρουνάκι - little pig) has its leaves eaten boiled by the locals.<ref>{{cite book |author=Κλεόνικος Γ. Σταυριδάκης [Kleonikos G. Stavridakis]  |trans-title= Wild edible plants of Crete | title=Η Άγρια βρώσιμη χλωρίδα της Κρήτης |publisher= Rethymnon Crete |year=2006 |isbn=960-631-179-1}}</ref> A south Italian variety of the species is also traditionally consumed by ethnic Albanians ([[Arbëreshë people]]) in the [[Vulture area]] (southern [[Italy]]). In the Arbëreshë communities in [[Lucania]] the young whorls of ''Centaurea calcitrapa'' are boiled and fried in mixtures with other weedy non cultivated greens.<ref>[http://www.andreapieroni.eu/Pieroni%20et%20al.,%202002d.pdf A. Pieroni, V. Janiak, C. M. Dürr, S. Lüdeke, E. Trachsel and M. Heinrich: In vitro Antioxidant Activity of Non-cultivated Vegetables of Ethnic Albanians in Southern Italy, Centre for Pharmacognosy and Phytotherapy, The School of Pharmacy, University of London 29-39 Brunswick Square, London WC1N 1AX, UK; PHYTOTHERAPY RESEARCH, 16, 467–473 (2002)]  {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110718171601/http://www.andreapieroni.eu/Pieroni%20et%20al.%2C%202002d.pdf |date=July 18, 2011 }}</ref>

==Control==
===Herbicides===
[[Picloram]] + [[2,4-Dichlorophenoxyacetic acid|2,4-D]], low volatile ester 2,4-D, [[Dicamba]], and [[Fluroxypyr]] + [[Aminopyralid]] are recommended for use in [[New South Wales]],<ref name="NSW-WeedWise">{{cite web | title=Star thistle (''Centaurea calcitrapa'') | website=NSW WeedWise, [[Department of Primary Industries (New South Wales)|Department of Primary Industries, New South Wales]], [[Australia]] | url=https://weeds.dpi.nsw.gov.au/Weeds/StarThistle | access-date=2021-03-03}}</ref> and [[aminocyclopyrachlor]] + [[chlorsulfuron]], [[aminopyralid]], chlorsulfuron, [[clopyralid]], clopyralid + 2,4-D, dicamba, [[diflufenzopyr]] + dicamba, picloram, and [[triclopyr]] + clopyralid for the [[Pacific Northwest]] of [[North America]].<ref name="PNWHB">{{cite web | title=Starthistle, yellow (''Centaurea solstitialis''), purple (''Centaurea calcitrapa''), and Iberian (''Centaurea iberica'') | website=Pacific Northwest Pest Management Handbooks | publisher=Pacific Northwest Extension ([[Oregon State University|Oregon]], [[Washington State University|Washington]], [[University of Idaho|Idaho]]) | date=2015-11-10 | url=http://pnwhandbooks.org/weed/problem-weeds/starthistle-yellow-centaurea-solstitialis-purple-centaurea-calcitrapa-iberian-centaurea-iberica | access-date=2021-03-03}}</ref>

====Herbicide resistance====
[[Picloram]] + [[2,4-Dichlorophenoxyacetic acid|2,4-D]], low volatile ester 2,4-D, [[Dicamba]], and [[Fluroxypyr]] + [[Aminopyralid]] all carry a "moderate" risk of producing [[herbicide resistance|resistance]] in ''C. calcitrapa''.<ref name="NSW-WeedWise" />

==Similar species==
* ''[[Centaurea aspera]]'', known as rough star-thistle. The main difference is the bract appendages are palmately arranged.
* ''[[Centaurea solstitialis]]'', known as yellow star thistle. Differs in having yellow flowers palmately arranged, spiny bract appendages, with middle spine only 1 to 2 cm.
